A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of SpikeLLM, including Appendix A.1–A.5. Text comparison and page rendering establish that only pages 1 and 9 differ; the remaining material is identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original SpikeLLM accuracy, perplexity, efficiency, and ablation results in Section 5, with additional experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the original SpikeLLM experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A, including repeated-training comparisons and additional quantization benchmarks.

M1.justification: GIF neurons, saliency-based spiking, Optimal Brain Spiking, and the ternary variant retain the same definitions, procedures, and training/inference mechanisms.

E1.justification: WikiText2, C4, the six zero-shot reasoning tasks, and the coverage of the appendix QLoRA and EfficientQAT experiments are unchanged. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: All reported comparisons retain their comparator membership. Table 5 already lists LLAMA-1-7B in both versions; correcting the accompanying baseline reference does not replace an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Training settings, model configurations, evaluation procedures, and ACE/Sparse ACE definitions are unchanged. Section 5.1 changes LLAMA-2-7B to LLAMA-7B to match the existing Table 5 context; the table retains both T=2 and T=4 configurations.

E4.justification: The GIF and saliency ablations in Figure 4, training-data robustness analysis in Figure 6, and structured versus unstructured comparison in Table 9 are identical.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2.2 retains the same 16 training trials with matched seeds for OmniQuant and SpikeLLM, and seed 2 for other experiments. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the efficiency finding: v2 describes 6.38× and 10.79× ACE savings for T=2/T=4 against LLAMA-2-7B; v3 reports 10.79× ACE and 6.38× Sparse ACE savings for T=2 against LLAMA-7B. These match the unchanged Table 5 ratios, 3886.22/360.20 and 3886.22/608.78. All tabulated and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 1 and its proof, equations, and Appendix A.4 equivalence arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about scaling spiking models to 7–70 billion parameters, compressing spike encoding, and improving on quantization.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, hardware implications, and applicability qualifications are retained. The stated performance gap from ANN LLMs and proposed benefit of continued pretraining remain unchanged; the efficiency edit corrects result attribution.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, calibration data instructions, hardware and training-time disclosures, and the code-access link are unchanged. The author email update does not alter resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, the reference list, and positioning relative to previous spiking and quantization methods are identical.

P1.justification: One efficiency paragraph is locally revised. The first page adds Zheng Liu's corresponding-author marker, updates contact information, and changes the arXiv version/date stamp. Section organization and the remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–12 retain their displays, captions, structure, and placement. The edits produce only local text rewrapping, without a change to page composition.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves a concrete inconsistency between Section 5.1 and Table 5 by correctly associating the 10.79× and 6.38× reductions with ACE and Sparse ACE for T=2 and correcting the baseline reference. This modestly improves reporting accuracy while retaining the scientific content and evidence.
